html:
SMTO-EXE-0188 — SMTO can't make this change without losing part of the document

GUID: ad5889cb-848f-57b9-9bee-355804b8a92f
Slug: office-unsupported-feature
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • Saving this change would have broken or silently dropped something in your file, such as a digital signature, merged cells, embedded objects or special formatting. SMTO stopped instead, so nothing was saved and your original is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the file is digitally signed, or the spreadsheet contains embedded objects such as an inserted document, make the change in Word, Excel or PowerPoint yourself. Any change would break the signature or lose the embedded object, so SMTO only reads these files.
  2. In Excel, unmerge the cells you want changed, or ask SMTO to use cells that aren't merged. Keep at least one other visible sheet before deleting a sheet. SMTO won't write into merged cells or leave a workbook with no visible sheet.
  3. In Word, ask SMTO to replace a shorter piece of text that has the same formatting throughout and contains no links, tracked changes or comments. SMTO only replaces text it can change without breaking its formatting or links.
  4. In PowerPoint, ask SMTO to use a slide layout that has a title and text box, or to change a shape that holds text. SMTO can only place text where the slide design has a place for it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new file it created, and the parts you care about, like signatures, merged cells and formatting, look right in it.

If it still fails

  • Make the change by hand in Word, Excel or PowerPoint. If you think SMTO should support it, select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and the change, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Office refused an edit that could not preserve a document feature: digital signatures, Excel embedded objects or unsupported extension metadata, merged cells, cross-run or complex Word text, commented content, missing title/text/notes placeholders, deleting the last visible sheet, or an unsupported cell value type.

What this means

  • Structural editing could not preserve signatures, embedded Excel objects, unsupported XML/merged structures, backend extension metadata or the requested object feature. Unsupported scalar/value types also fail safely. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Structural editing could not preserve signatures, embedded Excel objects, unsupported XML/merged structures, backend extension metadata or the requested object feature. Unsupported scalar/value types also fail safely.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific unsupported feature and whether a separate simpler copy or trusted application can preserve the requirement.

How to fix it

  • Identify the feature from the operation: signed packages and Excel files with embedded objects are read-only; openpyxl warnings during a write abort the save; Word replace must fall inside one plain run of a paragraph with no hyperlinks, fields or revisions; deletes cannot remove commented content; merged cells cannot be written; at least one visible sheet must remain; PowerPoint layouts need title/text placeholders. Edit in a trusted Office application or simplify the target, then rerun on a fresh revision.
  • Use a simpler document or edit in a trusted Office application. Cross-run Word replacement, signatures, merged-cell writes and unsupported backend features are rejected.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a simpler document or edit in a trusted Office application. Cross-run Word replacement, signatures, merged-cell writes and unsupported backend features are rejected.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported edit creates a separate verified output without silently dropping required document features.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
